binaries.name: fls
binaries.why: List files, deleted entries and named streams in an image. Invoked as an executable: CPL and IPL cannot be combined with AGPL in one work.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: icat
binaries.why: Extract a file by inode, including a named stream. Invoked as an executable: CPL and IPL cannot be combined with AGPL in one work.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: istat
binaries.why: Confirm an inode's size, timestamps and allocation before trusting an extract. Invoked as an executable: CPL and IPL cannot be combined with AGPL in one work.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: fsstat
binaries.why: Volume serial, cluster size and file system type. Invoked as an executable: CPL and IPL cannot be combined with AGPL in one work.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: mmls
binaries.why: Partition table, and the sector offset every other command needs. Invoked as an executable: CPL and IPL cannot be combined with AGPL in one work.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: ewfinfo
binaries.why: Read an E01's acquisition record and its stored digests.

binaries.name: ewfverify
binaries.why: Verify an E01 against the digest it stores, over the decoded media stream (the whole acquisition), where ewfinfo only prints the stored record. Same ewf-tools package as ewfinfo.

binaries.name: tsk_recover
binaries.why: Bulk recovery of deleted files from an image. Invoked as an executable.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: img_stat
binaries.why: The size and format of an image as The Sleuth Kit reads it, E01 included: the bound for a scan over the whole of it.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: img_cat
binaries.why: The raw bytes of an image, E01 included, over a range of sectors: a signature scan without converting the image first.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: mactime
binaries.why: Turn a Sleuth Kit body file into a MAC timeline (the disk-volumes recipe's timeline.csv). Invoked as an executable.
binaries.licence: CPL-1.0 core, IPL-1.0 in the TCT-derived parts

binaries.name: bdeinfo
binaries.why: Read a BitLocker volume header: encryption method and every key protector, before any key is known.

binaries.name: dislocker
binaries.why: Open a BitLocker volume as a file once a key or a clear-key protector is in hand. Invoked as an executable. Declared here so filesystem/encrypted can route to it; unlocking, and where its key comes from, is the encrypted-containers pack's method (which declares it too).

binaries.name: cryptsetup
binaries.why: Read a LUKS header and its key slots (luksDump). Opening a volume with a key is the encrypted-containers pack's method (which declares it too), not this pack's.

binaries.name: qemu-img
binaries.why: Convert a VHD, VHDX, VMDK or QCOW2 disk to raw, which is what the toolkit reads.

binaries.name: log2timeline
binaries.why: Build a super timeline from a whole image in one pass: every parser Plaso carries, into one storage file. Older packages install it as log2timeline.py; the tool accepts either. Pinned to plaso 20260720 with its whole dependency set in a hash lock (requires/locks/plaso.txt: a wheel hash per architecture where PyPI has one, and the sdist), so the image installs nothing else; the three programs share the one lock.

binaries.name: psort
binaries.why: Filter, sort and export a Plaso storage file. The half of a super timeline an examiner actually reads. Older packages install it as psort.py; the tool accepts either. Pinned to plaso 20260720 with its whole dependency set in a hash lock (requires/locks/plaso.txt: a wheel hash per architecture where PyPI has one, and the sdist), so the image installs nothing else; the three programs share the one lock.

binaries.name: pinfo
binaries.why: Print a Plaso storage file's own processing report: what each parser did, and the warnings and errors it raised. Older packages install it as pinfo.py. The disk-timeline recipe keeps its output as pinfo.txt, and a negative from a super timeline is read against it. Pinned to plaso 20260720 with its whole dependency set in a hash lock (requires/locks/plaso.txt: a wheel hash per architecture where PyPI has one, and the sdist), so the image installs nothing else; the three programs share the one lock.

binaries.name: bulk_extractor
binaries.why: Sweep a whole image for features at scale: addresses, URLs, card numbers, EXIF, and carved records, without a file system.

install.apt: built from source 2.2.0 (install.build): not packaged for Debian 12

binaries.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later for the code since 2015; the original NPS work is public domain; bundled third-party code keeps its own (unrar's among them)

binaries.name: photorec
binaries.why: Signature recovery over unallocated space, and a partition table a damaged disk no longer has.

binaries.name: target-query
binaries.why: One query interface over E01, VMDK, QCOW and a triage collection, with a plugin per artefact family. AGPL-3.0, the same licence as this harness. Pinned to the dissect metapackage 3.22 (dissect.target 3.25.1 and the dissect.* parsers it names) with its whole dependency set in a hash lock (requires/locks/dissect.txt: a wheel hash per architecture where PyPI has one, and the sdist).

binaries.name: luksdeinfo
binaries.why: Read a LUKS header and its key slots without unlocking the volume.

install.brew: https://github.com/libyal/libluksde (the library's own command-line tool, built from source; the PyPI package libluksde-python is the Python binding and does not install it)

binaries.name: fvdeinfo
binaries.why: Read the encryption metadata of a Core Storage (legacy FileVault 2) volume and its key material references. Not assumed to read an APFS volume: APFS structure is the macos-forensics pack's and the route into an encrypted APFS volume the encrypted-containers pack's.

install.brew: https://github.com/libyal/libfvde (the library's own command-line tool, built from source; the PyPI package libfvde-python is the Python binding and does not install it)

binaries.name: fsapfsinfo
binaries.why: Read an APFS container and its volumes, which the Sleuth Kit does not. Experimental libfsapfs: upstream does not support snapshots, Fusion drives or T2 encryption.

install.brew: https://github.com/libyal/libfsapfs (the library's own command-line tool, built from source; the PyPI package libfsapfs-python is the Python binding and does not install it)

binaries.name: pdftotext
binaries.why: The text of a PDF (-layout keeps its columns); pdfinfo, pdfimages and pdftohtml come in the same package.

binaries.name: ccl_indexeddb_dump
binaries.why: A Chromium or Electron IndexedDB (a chat client's, a web app's) read by database, object store and record; the ccl_chromium_reader library beside it, in /opt/dfir/src/ccl_indexeddb_dump/.venv/bin/python, also reads LevelDB, Local Storage, Session Storage and the cache. Brotli is held at 1.2.1 over the reader's old bound of 1.2.0, because before 1.2.1 the decoder (which reads content taken from the evidence) has an out-of-bounds write (GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35). Brotli 1.2.1 and zstd 1.5.7.2 install first from a hash lock (requires/locks/ccl_indexeddb_dump.txt: a file hash per architecture where PyPI has one, and the sdist). ccl_simplesnappy is not on PyPI and stays at its commit, an archive URL, outside the lock; its bytes are not hashed here.

binaries.name: steghide
binaries.why: Extract data hidden in a JPEG, BMP, WAV or AU file with steghide, given a passphrase the evidence supplies (an empty one included). It cannot tell a file with nothing hidden from one hidden under another passphrase: a negative is about that passphrase, and about steghide only.

binaries.name: exiftool
binaries.why: The metadata of a photo, a document or a media file (EXIF, XMP, PDF and Office properties), read without changing it. Installed by the base image; the mobile and document skills name it.

binaries.name: 7z
binaries.why: List the members of a 7z archive for the archive-members recipe, which calls the first of `7z`, `7zz`, `7za` and `7zr` it finds (archive_extract looks for the same four). Installed by the base image as p7zip-full. A RAR is read through the 7zz entry below, which archive_extract looks for first on a RAR.
binaries.licence: LGPL-2.1-or-later, with the unRAR licence restriction on the RAR code

binaries.name: 7zz
binaries.why: 7-Zip's own Linux console build (26.05, the build its download page links to, from the project's GitHub release), whose RAR codec reads RAR versions 4 and 5. archive_extract sends a RAR to it, listing with `7zz l -slt -ba` and extracting to a pipe, and looks for it before 7z, 7za and 7zr; it also lists and extracts a 7z. The base image's p7zip-full is a different build and is not relied on for RAR. The RAR codec is under 7-Zip's licence with the unRAR restriction: 7-Zip's License.txt says the unRAR sources cannot be used to re-create the RAR compression algorithm. Pinned by sha256 per architecture; it links the C++ runtime of the image (libstdc++6).
binaries.licence: LGPL-2.1-or-later, with the unRAR licence restriction on the RAR code; BSD-3-Clause and BSD-2-Clause for some code (7-Zip's License.txt for the Linux builds)
